line: Hi, I'm Ruth. I run the adult programs here: ESL, citizenship class, and a Thursday potluck that's mostly an excuse to meet people. Any of that useful?
Last month a retired judge and a woman who came over in 1998 found out they'd lived on the same block in Queens. That's the whole point. Bring anything, even chips.
I'm trying to get {homeCenter} to co-host something in the spring. Do you know {homeLeader} over there?
choice1: You should just walk over and ask her.

line: Honest question. When we print flyers in other languages, does anyone read them, or do they just make us feel good?
choice1: People read them. Put the date in big numbers.
choice2: Ask the people you want to come.

line: Thursday's potluck: I'd like you at the table with the three new families. You know how it feels to be new here. Will you come?
You seem to know people here and at {homeCenter}. Come to Thursday's potluck? I'd like you at the table with the new families.
Citizenship class attendance dropped by half this month. People won't write their address on a sign-up sheet anymore. I don't blame them.
choice1: Could they sign up without an address?
choice2: Maybe the class should meet somewhere else.

line: The federal grant came through. Two more ESL sections and money to book interpreters for the citizenship nights. I've been asking for that budget line for six years.
choice2: Who decides who gets the spots?

line: I hear you've been at {homeCenter} a lot. That's good. Tell them our doors are open too. Some days it feels like there's a wall down Grand Avenue.
choice2: People go where they feel comfortable.

line: Oh, hello. I won't keep you.
Sorry, I'm running between three things today. Catch me another day?
Hi, I'm Ruth, from the Elm Street Library. I'm leaving flyers for the citizenship class. The clinic gives me one corner of one table.
Tuesdays, Room 3. Twelve people. One is ninety and has read the Constitution more times than I have. We do a potluck Thursdays too. Bring anything, even chips.
choice1: Can I take a few flyers to hand out?

line: Ruth is restacking her flyers. Somebody has used the pile as a coaster again. "Every week. I'm going to start printing them on cardboard."
choice1: I'll take some for my building.
